_PARKED_DRAFT_playstation-ends-physical-:
NOT REVIEWED. Written by Claude as a format example, not by a GIES author. Rename this key to the bare slug only after an author has rewritten or approved it.

Sony ending physical disc production for new PlayStation releases in January 2028 is not a packaging decision, it is the removal of the last mechanism that let players own and resell a game. Discs were the only part of the console economy where value escaped the platform after the first sale. Once every new release is a licence, the second-hand market stops setting a floor under prices, and the publisher controls the discount calendar end to end.

The timing is the tell. Sony has said it does not plan to sell hardware at significant losses while it weighs PS6, and PlayStation hardware volumes are running at their weakest May in over two decades. A platform holder that can no longer subsidise boxes has to widen the margin on everything that comes after the box.

Watch what publishers do with launch pricing through 2027. If the disc exit is genuinely about cost, list prices should hold. If it is about margin capture, expect the floor to rise quietly first in the markets with the weakest resale culture.
